title: Debate Over INC Being A Safety Valve
definition: The historical and historiographical debate surrounding the foundation of the Indian National Congress (INC) in 1885, questioning whether it was engineered primarily as a 'safety valve' by British officials to defuse growing indigenous discontent or emerged organically from Indian national awakening.
importanceInUpsc: Crucial for UPSC Prelims (Modern Indian History chronology and historical interpretations) and Mains GS-1 (Freedom Struggle - its various stages and crucial contributors/controversies).
learningOutcomes: Master the core arguments of the Safety Valve Theory and its proponents.
Understand the counter-arguments, specifically the Conspiracy Theory and Lightning Conductor Theory.
Evaluate the nationalist interpretation championed by early nationalists and Marxist historians.
prerequisites: Foundational understanding of 19th-century socio-religious reform movements
Rise of regional political associations prior to 1885
